newsitem.title: USA: U.S. studying deep nuclear cuts under START-3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. studying deep nuclear cuts under START-3.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it was actively studying further deep cuts in nuclear warheads under a possible START-3 treaty with Russia, but stressed that Moscow must first ratify START-2.
The Defence Department said it was conducting a study of the impact of deep new strategic nuclear cuts as part of its quadrennial defence review of U.S. security policy.

But senior White House and defence officials said Russia's lower house of parliament, the Duma, must ratify the pending START-2 strategic arms reduction treaty to cut warheads on each side to 3,500 before START-3 could be settled.

The U.S. Senate ratified START-2 last year. But the Duma, worried about the cost of destroying weapons and angered at planned NATO expansion into Eastern and Central Europe, has so far refused to do so.

Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon told Reuters on Thursday that the Pentagon was studying warhead cuts in its defence review, but declined to confirm or deny a Washington Post report that warheads could be cut by another 1,000 to 1,500 on either side under START-3.
At the White House, spokesman Mike McCurry said, "First and foremost, what we are doing is encouraging the Russian Federation to achieve ratification of Start-2 in the Duma."
McCurry added that arms control experts on both sides "have always talked about additional strategic arms reductions that might be embraced in a Start-3 or 4."
He said arms control would be discussed by Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin at a Washington meeting Feb. 6-8.
The so-called Gore-Chernomyrdin Commission was formed to work on U.S.-Russian cooperation in a wide range of areas.
Outgoing U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, in a personal plea to the Duma last year, made clear that the United States was ready to embark on a START-3 treaty as soon as START-2 was ratified.

"This (Pentagon nuclear) review is something that is being conducted as part of the quadrennial defence review to determine how to prepare ourselves for the START-3 talks after the Russian Duma confirms START-2," Bacon told Reuters.
He said, however, that the study was part of the department's planned strategic review and had not being done as a carrot to encourage the Duma to ratify START-2.

Russia is not only worried about the cost of destroying warheads under START-2 but fears it will have to build new missiles in order to keep parity with the United States as Russia destroys big, multi-warheads weapons under the treaty.
But Perry told the Duma that such a problem could be addressed quickly by new cuts under START-3.
